races.name: Jack Frost Chiller & Freezer Hire Novices' Limited Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Character Testing
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer with solid good-ground form (2nd and 4th on good in last five), Mark Walford yard in quiet form (0/13 last 14 days), but Jamie Hamilton a competent pilot who can hunt a gap late; the 2m trip over hurdles at Uttoxeter suits a horse that travels well off a slow pace.

runners_data.name: Golden Circet
runners_data.note: Six-year-old hold-up type with a mixed recent record including a third last time out, Richie McLernon's experience of finding gaps in compressed finishes is a key asset; 47 days off could mean just enough freshening up though going marked unknown is a slight uncertainty.

runners_data.name: Colinski
runners_data.note: Four-year-old fitted with a p-style headgear, held up naturally but shown a placing over similar trips on good ground; Charlie Maggs claims 3lbs which is useful in a limited handicap, and the 32-day break looks straightforward enough.

runners_data.name: Daring To Dream
runners_data.note: Genuinely a hold-up horse by instinct but the density of similar types in this field means it will likely be closer to midfield than it wants; 84 days off is the most significant flag here, and the modest recent form figures (8-4-7-3-6) suggest this trip on good ground has not yet unlocked the best from Harriet Dickin's charge.

runners_data.name: Louie The Legend
runners_data.note: Consistent placer at 2m-plus on good ground (3rd twice in last five), Dylan Cunha's youngster has scope to improve and Tabitha Worsley's 7lb claim is a tangible weight advantage in a race run off a slow tempo; a genuine hold-up type who must navigate traffic.

runners_data.name: Karthala
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with four placings from five runs on good ground over hurdles — arguably the best course-profile in the field — but naturally a hold-up horse who will struggle to get into its preferred position with so many similar rivals; Jennie Candlish in strong recent form (4/21 last 14 days) is the standout trainer angle.

runners_data.name: Giddyupadingdong
runners_data.note: Neil Mulholland's six-year-old has a recent placing on good ground and holds a win over the trip, but is a genuine hold-up type squeezed toward the middle of the pack in this map; the STYLE_FIT tag (0.92) notes it is marginally less compromised than others, and Bradley Harris's 3lb claim helps on weight.

runners_data.name: Rapid Mission
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey horse returning from 95 days off — the longest absence in the field — and while there is a win in the form record, the recent figures (5-8-7-5-4) tell a story of modest consistency; genuine hold-up style now mapped centrally, meaning it must find a way through traffic it may not naturally navigate.

runners_data.name: Brenda Lady
runners_data.note: Three-run hurdles record on varying ground, Sean Bowen is a high-class booking for a horse rated just 79; naturally holds up but the limited recent form base (just three runs) makes her hard to evaluate with confidence, and she enters this race without an OR-boosting recent run.

runners_data.name: Battle Stride
runners_data.note: Four-year-old returning from 242 days off — a significant absence that is by far the most glaring fitness question in the race — and carries a warning flag for fading in finishes; hold-up horse mapped to midfield, but the combination of ring-rustiness and a tendency to weaken late makes this a very difficult win proposition.

runners_data.name: Littletown Lad
runners_data.note: Six-year-old with a string of poor finishes (7th, 8th, 6th, 10th, 10th in last five) who carries both a fades-in-finish flag and a redistribution to midfield; Jonathan England and Sam England are a reliable combination but the form record on good ground simply offers very little encouragement.

runners_data.name: Lady Fortune
runners_data.note: Unusually, a horse who has actually won over hurdles recently (form /5P-14), with a victory over 20f on good ground in the record; Isabelle Ryder's 5lb claim makes the weight attractive, and while naturally a hold-up type displaced centrally, the positive recent form separates her from most of this field.

runners_data.name: Granny B
runners_data.note: Lowest-rated runner in the field at OR 73, hold-up style mapped to midfield, and the form figures (8-6-3-?-5) include one placing but are generally modest; Kevin Brogan is an experienced jumps rider but Michael Mullineaux's yard is quiet (0/2 last 14 days), and this looks a very tough assignment.

races.paceDynamic: This is a thoroughgoing hold-up race with no confirmed front-runner across all 13 runners, meaning the early gallop is likely to be cautious and the field will bunch together through the middle stages of the 2m trip at Uttoxeter. Without any horse willing to set a true tempo, the race will almost certainly compress into a sprint finish from the home turn, where positional luck, jumping fluency at the final hurdles, and a late burst will matter most. The field holds considerably more hold-up types than the race map can accommodate at the rear — Karthala, Daring To Dream, Giddyupadingdong, Rapid Mission, and Brenda Lady are all genuine hold-up horses displaced into midfield on the map because there is simply no room for them all to fulfil their natural roles. In a race run at a false or dawdling pace, the advantage tilts firmly toward horses who can travel smoothly in a compact field, find a clear passage in the home straight, and finish powerfully — those with the best recent form on good ground and the most fluent jumping credentials stand to benefit most.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Slow Pace Bunched Sprint
scenarios.trigger: If no horse establishes even a modest lead early and the field crawls for the first mile before a scramble erupts from the second-last.
scenarios.body: The entire field will be tightly grouped approaching two out, making jumping errors potentially catastrophic, and the winner will emerge from whoever finds the cleanest run from the home turn; horses with tactical speed and good hurdle technique over this 2m trip at Uttoxeter are ideally placed.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Competitive Moderate Pace
scenarios.trigger: If a couple of horses push forward slightly faster than the field expects, stretching the field into a more conventional shape by halfway.
scenarios.body: A genuine gallop suits horses who can travel with the pace from a prominent position and quicken again late; the race becomes more of a test of stamina-speed combination over the 2m trip.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Front Runner Emerges Unopposed
scenarios.trigger: If one horse breaks unexpectedly clear from the pack early and is allowed to bowl along unchallenged on good ground.
scenarios.body: A lone leader can dictate a comfortable rhythm, conserve energy, and sprint clear from the last hurdle; any horse willing to race more prominently than its usual style would find themselves with a significant positional advantage.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Closers Land Late
scenarios.trigger: If the pace is just strong enough to stretch the field and genuine hold-up horses find daylight in the straight to produce a sustained late run.
scenarios.body: A true staying closer who can pick off tiring rivals in the final 100 yards would benefit, though this scenario is tempered by the fact that so many of the natural hold-up horses in this field have been mapped out of their preferred position and may not be racing in their ideal style.

watchPoints.text: Karthala's trainer Jennie Candlish is in strong recent form (4/21 last 14 days) and this horse has placed in four of five runs on good ground — watch for Sean Quinlan to hunt a prominent pitch whatever the map suggests.

Lady Fortune is the standout positive form angle with a recent win over the trip on good ground and Sean Bowen-level jockey in Isabelle Ryder (5lb claim) — watch for an aggressive ride that attempts to overcome the hold-up redistribution.
Battle Stride returns from 242 days off with a fades-in-finish flag attached — if it shows early in the race that it is ring-rusty or labours at the hurdles, it is a horse to leave alone entirely.

With no front-runner confirmed, watch the first two hurdles: if the field crawls and the pace is genuinely false, horses drawn toward the outside rail may get stuck in a wall of traffic turning for home and never find daylight.

Colinski's headgear (p) represents a first-time or recent application — in a compressed, bunched race where tactical sharpness matters, any improvement in focus or concentration from the headgear switch could make the 3lb claim from Charlie Maggs particularly potent.

races.name: Bravo Benefits Celebrations Novices' Limited Handicap Steeple Chase (gbb Race)

runners_data.name: Sony Bill
runners_data.note: Confirmed front runner with Harry Cobden booked — a notable upgrade in jockey quality — and 17 days since last run; good-ground form reads 5/14 on similar going with zero wins suggesting he fronts up but gets overhauled, and the style fit score of 0.93 indicates he is slightly racing out of his best role as a pure leader rather than a tracking type.

runners_data.name: La Pinsonniere
runners_data.note: Nicky Henderson sends this six-year-old 0/2 in the trainer's 14-day window but the horse's five placed efforts on similar going (0W5P) confirm consistent prominence; jumps clean and the 21f–26f Goodwood and Uttoxeter form on good ground suits the conditions perfectly, and being the likeliest horse to secure the tracking berth directly behind Sony Bill is the key positional advantage here.

runners_data.name: Sunray Shadow
runners_data.note: Five wins and seven places in sim-going conditions (5W7P) tell a strong story — this horse is in prime form and genuinely thrives on good ground — but the redistribution note is real: with Sony Bill and La Pinsonniere also wanting prominent ground, Sunray Shadow may find themselves racing further back than ideal, tempering what would otherwise be a very strong profile; headgear (tp) suggests a horse who needs to be switched on from the front.

runners_data.name: Samuel Spade
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse trained by Ben Pauling, ridden by a 5lb claimer in a four-runner field where a modest pace is probable — the worst possible combination for a closer needing a strong gallop to close; one win at 23f on good ground hints at ability, but recent form (88-415) and structural disadvantage in this race shape make him reliant on a scenario that is unlikely to materialise.

races.paceDynamic: Sony Bill is the confirmed front runner and will set the tempo from the off over this 3m Uttoxeter chase, with La Pinsonniere and Sunray Shadow both natural prominent types pressing for the same ground behind him — only one or two can genuinely occupy those early positions, meaning Sunray Shadow is the likeliest to be shuffled back from their preferred spot. Sony Bill, uncontested in front, should dictate a controlled, sustainable gallop that does not overly punish those racing prominently but denies a true late swoop from hold-up horses. Samuel Spade, as the sole genuine hold-up horse in a small field, will be anchored at the rear with ground to make up in the straight. This race shape strongly favours the prominent/tracking profile — specifically those able to travel close to Sony Bill's pace and strike when the front runner's stamina is tested in the final mile — with true hold-up tactics likely starved of the strong gallop needed to close late. The field holds more prominent types than can all secure their favoured position, and La Pinsonniere is likeliest to actually claim the slot closest to Sony Bill, with Sunray Shadow the one most at risk of being shuffled back.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front, Prominent Pounce
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill dictates an uncontested, measured pace and a tracking horse picks him off approaching the last.
scenarios.body: Sony Bill sets a manageable tempo throughout, and the horse travelling most fluently just off the pace — likely La Pinsonniere or Sunray Shadow if they recover their position — strikes as the leader fades after the third-last; a small, slow field at Uttoxeter over 3m suits a patient stalker who jumps cleanly.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Sony Bill Gallops Clear
scenarios.trigger: If Sony Bill's front-running trip translates into an unassailable lead and none of the prominent horses can bridge the gap in the straight.
scenarios.body: Sony Bill's handlers aim at this race specifically (17 days fresh, Harry Cobden booked) and if the pace is truly relaxed in front he could jump and travel his way to a comfortable success; prominent rivals burning petrol chasing him without landing a blow would leave the hold-up horse with too much to do.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Prominent Scrimmage Blows Field
scenarios.trigger: If the three prominent/front types fight for position early, lifting the tempo and sapping stamina across the field before the home straight.
scenarios.body: A contested early gallop over 3m on good ground could compromise all three up-with-the-pace horses — Sony Bill, La Pinsonniere, and Sunray Shadow — opening a window for the hold-up Samuel Spade to reel them in; Beau Morgan (claim) needs to time the move precisely and Samuel Spade's sketchy form figures make this a low-probability lifeline.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Late-Run Closer Swamps
scenarios.trigger: If a genuinely fast pace develops and Samuel Spade produces an atypical strong late run to catch a tiring front group.
scenarios.body: Samuel Spade has won over this trip and on good ground before, but his recent form figures (88-415) and hold-up style in a slow-tempo small field make a winning late swoop unlikely; this scenario depends on conditions breaking against the pace-setters in a way the evidence does not strongly support.

watchPoints.text: Sony Bill — if Harry Cobden immediately sends him to the front and builds a lead of five or more lengths by the halfway point, the race shape locks in around him and all rivals face a flat-out pursuit rather than a controlled stalk.

Sunray Shadow — watch the first two furlongs for a scrimmage if both La Pinsonniere and Sunray Shadow press for the same prominent ground; if Sunray Shadow is forced wide or back, their effective running style for the race changes materially.
La Pinsonniere — has headgear flag (hg:p) and a 33-day break; if jumping is rusty or the horse is ring-rusty, it surrenders the key stalking position and the race shape collapses to a Sony Bill solo.

Samuel Spade — Beau Morgan's 5lb claim is worth monitoring: if Morgan attempts to ride more positively than the H style suggests to avoid being isolated at the back of a four-runner field, it could compress the shape unexpectedly.

Going unknown across all Uttoxeter runners — if the track rides slower or softer than anticipated, the advantage shifts marginally toward Samuel Spade's stamina base, but Sony Bill's good-ground metrics (3/20f/GOO) and La Pinsonniere's five placed runs on similar conditions remain the benchmark.

races.name: Sun Racing The Favourite Pullout Every Day Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Romany Brown
runners_data.note: Sets off in front and is confirmed as the race's sole pacesetter; sim-going record of 8/9 on similar ground is excellent, but 254 days off the track is a material concern, and racing as P rather than an outright lead role suggests connections may let him stride on rather than dictate — confidence in his stamina to hold on is the key question.

runners_data.name: An Bradan Feasa
runners_data.note: Consistent form string with three wins from 15 similar-ground starts and a recent third 27 days ago; Tom Bellamy's booking is positive, and the 16f trip at Uttoxeter on good suits perfectly — should secure a prominent pitch and is the horse most likely to be travelling best when the race is decided.

runners_data.name: King Ulanda
runners_data.note: Won over 18f at good going in his recent history and has course-distance form; Jack Tudor rides, headgear (tp) suggests he needs restraining, and his recent PF6-14 form string including a fall means confidence needs rebuilding — five similar-ground runs producing two wins is an encouraging profile if he jumps cleanly.

runners_data.name: Machete Beach
runners_data.note: Three wins from five good-ground starts underlines his quality, and he arrives in form having won two of his last three; his natural game is to race prominently, but with Romany Brown, An Bradan Feasa, and King Ulanda all ahead of him in the positional queue, Gavin Sheehan will likely have to settle for a position behind where this horse operates best.

runners_data.name: Ip Up
runners_data.note: Genuine hold-up horse wearing a hood, last seen winning over this exact 16f trip on good going; Jedd O'Keeffe's 14-day strike rate is modest and 33 days off the track is fine, but he needs the pace to be genuine enough for his closing run to have real meaning given the controlled tempo Romany Brown is likely to set.

runners_data.name: Ask A Sainte
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride for Olly Murphy, whose 14-day figures (3/16) are decent; Ask A Sainte's true game is to race prominently, and with a 2/1/4/5/4 recent record he is clearly competitive at this level — but finishing behind Romany Brown, An Bradan Feasa, and King Ulanda for early position means he is likely to race in a spot that doesn't play to his strengths today.

runners_data.name: St Just In Time
runners_data.note: Harry Derham's yard has no recent 14-day runners to assess; the form string (94342/) includes a slash suggesting a break and his sim-going record on good is sparse at 0 wins from 4 placed, meaning he is unproven as a genuine contender here — a hold-up type at 2m who needs others to do his donkey work and the field to come back to him.

races.paceDynamic: Romany Brown is the one confirmed front-runner here and should enjoy an uncontested lead, setting a controlled, sustainable gallop over 2m on good ground at Uttoxeter. Behind him, An Bradan Feasa and King Ulanda will push for prominent positions, creating a genuine cluster vying for the first two slots off the pace. This field holds more front-running and prominent types than can all secure their natural position — Machete Beach and Ask A Sainte are genuine prominent racers but are mapped to midfield because the real estate up front is already taken, meaning they face a tactical compromise they may not overcome. With Romany Brown dictating an honest but unforced tempo, the race shape most favours horses who can travel just behind the leader and produce their effort from a position of comfort — making prominent-to-mid types who genuinely get their position the primary beneficiaries, while true hold-up horses Ip Up and St Just In Time will need the pace to lift significantly in the final half-mile.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Romany Brown Controls
scenarios.trigger: If Romany Brown gets to the front unchallenged and sets a measured, self-paced gallop that stretches the field without burning petrol.
scenarios.body: Romany Brown dictates from the front with no one willing to commit to chasing him hard, meaning the race is run at a tempo that suits horses who travel fluidly in behind; An Bradan Feasa and King Ulanda, pressing from prominent positions, are best placed to strike when the real test arrives at the final hurdle.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Pace Hots Up Mid-Race
scenarios.trigger: If An Bradan Feasa or King Ulanda press Romany Brown hard enough from the second hurdle to force a genuinely searching gallop.
scenarios.body: A faster-run race compresses the mid-division and puts Romany Brown under pressure earlier than ideal, increasing the chance of a prominent-to-midfield horse landing a late blow; Machete Beach, if he has tracked closer than his mapped position suggests, has the form to capitalise on a pace-pressured leader.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Hold-Up Horse Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace proves strong enough throughout to set up a sustained, testing finish where hold-up horses can utilise superior reserves.
scenarios.body: Ip Up, a winner over this exact trip and going combination, would be the primary beneficiary, closing from the rear as the prominent horses spend their energy fighting for position; St Just In Time's hold-up style is less proven over this distance but a genuine end-to-end gallop is the one scenario that brings him into play.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Tactical Lottery
scenarios.trigger: If Romany Brown is challenged early, the field bunches, and the race breaks down into a ragged contest with no genuine rhythm.
scenarios.body: Positional chaos would strip Romany Brown of his advantage and level the field, potentially benefiting Ask A Sainte if he can recover to a prominent role — though his style-fit concern means this is a low-confidence scenario; An Bradan Feasa's consistency and class edge give him residual claims even in a messy race.

watchPoints.text: Romany Brown's 254-day absence is the biggest single risk to Scenario A — if he shows any ring rust at the first or second hurdle, the whole pace structure collapses.

Machete Beach and Ask A Sainte are both genuine prominent racers who will be jostling for a position they cannot both hold — watch the first two flights for a scramble that could unsettle either runner and shuffle the race order unexpectedly.

King Ulanda's recent fall (F in form string) combined with tp headgear makes his jumping reliability a watch point — a jumping error from him in the early stages could affect the prominent group given the compressed nature of this 7-runner field.

Ip Up's win came over this exact course and distance on good going — if Romany Brown sets a stronger pace than expected, he becomes materially more dangerous from the rear and his odds may not fully reflect that upside.

An Bradan Feasa's trainer Jack Jones runs at a 2/13 14-day strike rate — not a barn in flying form, but the horse's own consistency and going/trip profile are strong enough that this is merely a note to file rather than a reason to dismiss.

races.name: Alfie Flatt 18th Birthday Celebration Handicap Steeple Chase (ARC Summer Chase Series Qualifier) (GBB Race)

runners_data.name: Theonlywayiswessex
runners_data.note: Alan King's eight-year-old has strong form in similar good-ground conditions (11/15 sim-going, two wins at the trip) and Tom Bellamy should exploit the lack of pace rivals to control this race from the front; 42 days since last run is not a concern given the trainer's seasonal pattern, though racing at the top of the weights at 163lbs over 2m4f will test stamina late on.

runners_data.name: Pep Talking
runners_data.note: Billy Aprahamian's yard is in sharp form (1/2 over the past 14 days) and Pep Talking's consistent record — five wins from 15 similar-going runs and placed twice at this trip — makes it the most natural threat to the favourite; Gavin Sheehan can slot in second and make a clean challenge without over-committing early.

runners_data.name: Ukantango
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen partners a genuine hold-up performer who has won twice from the back in soft conditions, but the absence of true pace pressure in a five-runner field makes it hard for Ukantango to manufacture the late gaps needed; headgear (tp) suggests the yard wants more focus and the 54-day break is worth noting, though Olly Murphy's horses often return fresh.

runners_data.name: Le Gentleman
runners_data.note: Jack Tudor's young five-year-old is by instinct a front-running type but the crowded nature of the prominent positions means he is likely to find himself racing further back than ideal; recent good-ground form is solid (2/5 sim-going, one win at the trip) and the 19-day turnaround is sharp, suggesting trainer confidence, though racing against his grain limits the ceiling.

runners_data.name: My Friend Sean
runners_data.note: Tom Lacey's seven-year-old has been running well below his best in recent outings (form string 6636-5) and, like Le Gentleman, his natural prominence means he will be squeezed away from his preferred position; headgear (tp) is in place to sharpen him up but Stan Sheppard will have to ride a patient race that does not suit, and the sim-going record of 9/15 is the weakest in the field.

races.paceDynamic: Theonlywayiswessex is the lone confirmed front-runner here and, with no genuine rival to pressure them from the gate, Tom Bellamy can dictate a measured, sustainable gallop over this 2m4f trip at Uttoxeter. Pep Talking is a natural prominent type who will look to sit close to the pace rather than lead, creating a small cluster at the front but not a battle for supremacy. This field holds more prominent-running types than the shape can accommodate — Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean are both genuine front-rank horses by instinct but are mapped to midfield because Theonlywayiswessex and Pep Talking are most likely to actually secure the forward positions. The uncontested, controlled pace set by Theonlywayiswessex benefits prominent-to-midfield stalkers who can travel economically before unleashing their finish, and Ukantango — the only true hold-up runner — will need the pace to genuinely collapse late to make a winning challenge.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Controlled Front Sets It Up
scenarios.trigger: If Theonlywayiswessex dictates without serious early pressure and the pace remains even throughout.
scenarios.body: Bellamy controls the tempo and the field strings out tamely, leaving the front pair to battle it out from two out with Pep Talking the most likely challenger having stalked throughout; horses who travel close to the pace into the home straight are best placed to pounce.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalker Pounces
scenarios.trigger: If Pep Talking tracks smoothly and overpowers Theonlywayiswessex in the final half-mile.
scenarios.body: Gavin Sheehan times his challenge to sweep past the leader from the last fence, with Pep Talking's strong record in similar going (12/15 sim-going, five wins) underpinning confidence; horses held up late will struggle to close on a winner who has already committed.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Closer Swamps Tired Leaders
scenarios.trigger: If the front-runners set a genuinely testing gallop that causes them to fade in the final furlong.
scenarios.body: Ukantango, the only natural hold-up horse in the field, would be the beneficiary if the pace is fast enough to exhaust the prominently-placed runners; however, Sean Bowen needs a more searching tempo than is likely given the small field and Theonlywayiswessex's ability to control proceedings.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Chaos Disrupts Shape
scenarios.trigger: If a jumping error, falling horse, or dramatic change in pace scrambles the field order early.
scenarios.body: With only five runners, any incident at a fence could reshuffle all positions and bring the out-of-role prominent horses — Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean — back into contention having been forced to adapt their tactics; this remains a low-probability outcome but the small field means any incident has an outsized effect.

watchPoints.text: Theonlywayiswessex sets the only meaningful pace — if Bellamy elects to bowl along unchallenged, the entire race shape collapses into a test of which rival can overhaul a leader on their own terms.

Le Gentleman and My Friend Sean are both wired to race forward but cannot both do so — watch the first two furlongs to see which, if either, makes a play for position and forces an unplanned pace duel.
Ukantango's hold-up profile is only viable if the front-runners accelerate enough to tire; in a small field with a measured gallop, Bowen may find himself with no gaps to exploit turning for home.

Pep Talking's headgear flag (hg:p) is worth monitoring at the start — if the horse dwells or gets outpaced early, its ability to stalk Theonlywayiswessex throughout, the key to its chance, could be undermined.

With going listed as unknown across the board, any deterioration from the nominal Good surface would most likely benefit Ukantango, whose sim-going wins include soft-ground performances, and least benefit Theonlywayiswessex whose record is overwhelmingly good-ground based.

races.name: Sun Racing Summer Jumps Championship Mares' Handicap Hurdle Race

runners_data.name: Hello Cello
runners_data.note: Hold-up performer for Harry Fry with only 17 days between runs; has placed twice in similar going but no wins in that sample (0W2P on good), and the 2m7½f trip is on the outer edge of her proven range — needs something to go wrong at the front to land a blow from the back.

runners_data.name: Kayla's Friend
runners_data.note: Sean Bowen takes the ride on this confirmed front-runner whose STYLE_FIT flag suggests she may find it harder to dominate here than in smaller fields; Olly Murphy yard in solid form (3/16 in 14 days) and she has a recent win at 2m on good, though stepping up in trip is the key unknown.

runners_data.name: Camshaft
runners_data.note: Jonjo O'Neill Jr. aboard a five-year-old who has won twice in his last four outings including a 23f success on good — the form and trip metrics align well; likely to press forward and is the most progressive horse in the prominent group on raw trajectory.

runners_data.name: Blackwater Lilly
runners_data.note: Consistent hold-up performer who has placed in good-ground races before but is locked on four consecutive fourths — winning form appears elusive; Neil King's yard is quiet (0/2 in 14 days) and no headgear change suggests this is a straightforward entry rather than a freshened preparation.

runners_data.name: Grey Gamble
runners_data.note: Unresolved style (U-tagged) for Emma Lavelle who has had a quiet recent spell (0/3); the horse has no wins or placings in simulated similar going (0W0P) and five-year-olds tackling 2m7½f on this evidence are not guaranteed to stay — tactically awkward to place.

runners_data.name: Theirshegoes
runners_data.note: Nine-year-old hold-up type partnered by claimer Joshua Thompson (5lb), trainer has had no runners in the past fortnight; form string of 845-78 shows no placings in recent outings and the combination of age, weight, and junior jockey makes this one of the more speculative entries in the field.

runners_data.name: Faerie Cutlass
runners_data.note: Kim Bailey and Mat Nicholls-trained eight-year-old wearing tongue-strap; off 53 days and the form (U467-7) has been poor, but she is a natural prominent type on a good-ground course where her best figures have come — needs a career-best to be relevant.

runners_data.name: Belladinotte
runners_data.note: Sara Ender runner with two career wins both over 24f on good ground, making the trip and going combination genuinely relevant; Harry Bannister a competent partner and the 1/3 trainer strike in 14 days is modest but live — one of the few hold-up-to-prominent types whose form profile suits the conditions precisely.

runners_data.name: Athena's Dream
runners_data.note: Four-year-old with unresolved style for Harriet Dickin, running off 19 days with cheekpieces listed; placed twice on similar going (0W2P), trending upward in form (674-23), and the drop in weight compared to rivals is a practical advantage — youth and improving profile are the angles here.

runners_data.name: Global Hideaway
runners_data.note: Christian Williams runner fresh off a 12-day break who is at heart a hold-up horse, though the redistribution note reflects that the rear of this field is crowded — his natural berth at the back may be harder to exploit than usual; OR 75 is lowest in the field and the form (8P-95) gives little encouragement at this level regardless of positioning.

races.paceDynamic: Kayla's Friend is the one confirmed front-runner in this field and, with no genuine rival likely to push her from the front over 2m7½f on good ground, she should control proceedings at a sustainable, measured tempo from the outset. Camshaft and Faerie Cutlass are prominent types who will want to sit just off the pace, while Belladinotte may also push forward, creating a small group tracking Kayla's Friend through the early stages rather than a lone leader racing in isolation. That controlled gallop over this staying trip is unlikely to stretch the field dramatically early, meaning the race will be set up as a test of jumping fluency and late stamina rather than raw pace — a shape that classically favours horses with the ability to travel prominently or make a smooth move from mid-division rather than those relying on a true end-to-end slog to bring closers into it. The field holds more hold-up types than the map can accommodate at the rear: Global Hideaway is a genuine hold-up horse redistributed into midfield, meaning the backmarkers' group is less pure than it appears, and those horses are less likely to get a true rails-hugging, ground-saving passage. Prominent movers and progressive types who can travel smoothly into contention off a steady early clip are the primary beneficiaries of this shape.

scenarios.label: A
scenarios.title: Kayla's Friend Controls Throughout
scenarios.trigger: If Kayla's Friend is allowed to stride on uncontested and sets a genuine but unhurried pace that she can sustain to the last hurdle.
scenarios.body: Kayla's Friend dictates every yard at a tempo that suits her stamina profile, with Camshaft and Faerie Cutlass tracking respectfully but never applying pressure, and the race becomes a test of who can quicken from a compact group off the final bend; horses close to the pace who jump fluently hold a decisive positional advantage.

scenarios.label: B
scenarios.title: Prominent Stalkers Pounce Late
scenarios.trigger: If Kayla's Friend fades approaching the last and one of the prominent stalkers picks up to score with a clean round of jumping.
scenarios.body: The controlled early fractions mean Camshaft or Belladinotte will have been travelling within themselves, and a fluent jump at the final hurdle allows them to sprint clear of a tiring leader; this shape rewards horses that have been saving energy in the prominent group rather than those forced wide or ridden with patience from further back.

scenarios.label: C
scenarios.title: Midfield Finisher Swoops
scenarios.trigger: If the pace collapses in the straight and the front group ties up, allowing a well-positioned mid-division runner to reel them in.
scenarios.body: Hello Cello or Athena's Dream, both capable of producing a measured late run, could catch a tired front group if the race develops any real tempo through the middle section; this scenario requires the early pace to have been genuinely taxing enough to expose stamina limitations at the top of the weights, which is far from certain given Kayla's Friend's likely controlled approach.

scenarios.label: D
scenarios.title: Pace Collapse, Outsider Benefits
scenarios.trigger: If the race falls apart tactically with multiple fallers or a wholesale pace collapse and a fresher lower-rated runner capitalises.
scenarios.body: Global Hideaway, though not a natural midfield type, could benefit from complete chaos at the front that renders positional tactics irrelevant; this is a low-probability outcome entirely dependent on adverse jumping incidents or a race run in an unusually erratic manner that negates the advantage of the better-positioned horses.

watchPoints.text: Camshaft has won two of his last four over trips including 23f on good ground — if he travels smoothly off Kayla's Friend's shoulder and jumps cleanly at the last, he represents the most credible threat to the front-runner.

Kayla's Friend's STYLE_FIT flag (0.93) is a genuine caution: if this larger field crowds her early, she may not achieve her natural front-running position as cleanly as expected, which could scramble the whole pace dynamic.

Belladinotte's two career wins have both come at exactly 24f on good ground — the trip reduction to 2m7½f (23f) is marginal but worth monitoring if she appears to find the run home easier than rivals suggest.

Global Hideaway has run just 12 days ago and Christian Williams has had zero winners from six runners in the past fortnight — combining recency with yard form makes this runner one to watch for early market drift rather than support.

Three of the prominent group — Camshaft, Faerie Cutlass, and Belladinotte — are all 53, 53, and 24 days since their last run respectively; the fresher horses in this spot could find the first mile comfortable but may not be wound up to peak fitness, worth watching in-running for signs of blowing early.
